messages:
ashley: heads-up — customer X reported a spike that exhausted their Dedicated pool and our spillover routed them to hosted. They flagged data isolation concerns and anomalous billing. Can we review routing guarantees?

mike: thanks. do we have logs for that tenant? curious whether policy allowed spillover or we forced it due to capacity.

ashley: yes, attached snippets below. spillover was triggered by policy 'dedicated:best_effort' which allows hosted fallback when headroom < 5%.

ashley: ```json
{"tenant":"cust-x","route_decision":"spillover","dedicated_headroom_pct":3.4,"fallback_model":"gpt-3.8-q8"}
```

sara: oof — two concerns: (1) for regulated tenants, even metadata in hosted logs may be unacceptable, (2) billing tooltip in console showed the hosted model cost but not the 'was routed from dedicated' context.

james: second point: our console UX doesn't call out fallbacks in the per-route cost breakdown. we just attribute tokens to the model used. customers need lineage: which requests hit Dedicated vs Hosted vs Variant.

nev: question — was the fallback to a 'compatible' model variant, or any available hosted model? routing code picks compatible by architecture + seq_len, but there was a recent change that widened compatibility to quantized variants.

mike: looking at the policy commit (PR #4587) — policy default is: { "on_dedicated_exhaustion": "spillover_if_compatible", "compatibility_tolerance": "arch+seq+quantization_relaxed" }

ashley: That 'relaxed' bit is the problem. For some tenants we want strict isolation: either no spillover, or spillover only to same-privacy-class hosted nodes (e.g., encrypted). Also model-variant downgrading (eg fp16->int8) can change output characteristics.

sara: Agreed. Propose we add two axes to policy: tier-based isolation and variant-strictness. Example policy snippet: 

```yaml
routing_policy: 
  tier: enterprise
  on_dedicated_exhaustion: block_or_queue
  fallback_allowed: false
  notify_on_block: true

routing_policy: 
  tier: standard
  on_dedicated_exhaustion: spillover
  fallback_allowed: true
  variant_strictness: strict  # options: strict, relaxed
```

james: I like explicit tiers. Also need runtime flags so we can flip behavior during outages without a full rollout.

nev: +1 runtime flags. Also, telemetry: any routed request should carry headers: X-Route-Origin (dedicated|hosted), X-Model-Variant, X-Fallback-Reason. That makes console traces and audits deterministic.

mike: we already have X-Model and X-Instance, but not an explicit origin. easy add. what about backfilling for past events? we should retro-tag logs where possible but at least ensure future requests are annotated.

ashley: for billing, need an explicit line item in usage: 'tokens_routed_from_dedicated_to_hosted' so invoices show blocked credits or cross-billing instead of attributing solely to hosted. Legal asked for this.

james: does this affect SLA credits? if we spillover and latency degrades, tenant expects SLA protections. Should landing in hosted trigger a different SLA calc.

nev: yeah, SLA should be computed per-request by origin. If count(hosted) > threshold while tenant on Dedicated plan => auto-sla-adjust and alert CS.

sara: UX ask: console route timeline on the model dashboard — show per-request dots with color: green (dedicated), orange (fallback variant), red (blocked). Hover shows headers above.

mike: implementation notes: 
- policy evaluation happens at routing stage (pre-scheduling).
- when capacity tight, we sample decisions for telemetry to avoid 10x log volume.
- require a config knob: tenant_policy_overrides (applies per-tenant).

ashley: sample routing pseudo-code: 
```python
# pre-routing
policy = get_policy(tenant)
if policy.on_dedicated_exhaustion == 'block_or_queue' and dedicated_headroom < policy.threshold:
    return block_request()
if policy.on_dedicated_exhaustion == 'spillover' and policy.fallback_allowed:
    candidate = find_compatible(hosted_pool, strict=policy.variant_strictness=='strict')
    if candidate:
        annotate(headers, origin='hosted', fallback_reason='dedicated_exhaustion')
        return route_to(candidate)
    else:
        return queue_or_block()
```

nev: question — find_compatible needs to expose a compatibility score so we can decide 'best fit' and record if quantization changed. store model_variant_diff in telemetry.

james: ops-bot: can we get a temp flag to turn off 'relaxed quantization' for all enterprise tenants?

ops-bot: @james — flag created: routing.disable_relaxed_quantization.enterprise = true. Will be honored by the routing service within 30s. :white_check_mark:

ashley: thanks. next steps: (1) add X-Route-Origin & X-Fallback-Reason headers (mike), (2) policy schema change + runtime flag (sara + james), (3) console telemetry UI: route timeline + invoice line (product + billing), (4) SLA calc per-origin (nev).

mike: I'll open a PR for header + telemetry schema and add sampling controls.

sara: I'll draft policy schema and a migration plan; want to avoid surprising customers when we flip defaults.

james: I'll coordinate with CS + legal about billing line and SLA wording.

nev: I'll add telemetry fields for model_variant_diff and compatibility_score. plus an alert when >10% of Dedicated requests are spilled in 5m.

ashley: awesome. please add short notes to the routing RFC so we have an audit trail. Also put a small notice in the console for any tenant impacted this week.

mike: will do. thanks all. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Reminder: deploy of routing-service annotator scheduled at 2026-03-19T02:15Z.

ashley: noted. ping if any rollback is needed.
